solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Civilisation's plunging into frenzied …

definitions.note: an adjective, as the answer is

parts.note: the Inca civilisation of Peru; its adjective, 'of that civilisation', is Incan
a descent is a plunge or drop downwards

explanation.surface: A whole civilisation sinks into some frenzied state, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a link word, not an insertion: the two pieces simply sit side by side. The ellipsis joins the surface to 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone white-hot with rage is wild and beside themselves, which is what frenzied describes.

clue.text: Superb actor in variety leaving commentaries for 'Review'

indicators.note: in variety says the letters of actor may come in any order, not as one block
leaving means those letters are taken away from the longer word
Review read as re-view, looking again in a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A superb actor in a variety show moves from writing commentaries to a review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the letters of ACTOR, scattered, from COMMENTARIES, leaving MMENIES, which 'Review' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is used informally to mean excellent or terrific, much like superb.

clue.text: Mark, look, steer's corralled

indicators.note: corralled means penned in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to con a ship is to steer it
lo is an old word for look!

explanation.surface: Look, a steer has been rounded up into a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' is not the bullock but the verb, to direct a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark.

clue.text: Some of life's essentials — nothing French — included in crazy stunt

indicators.note: included in means put inside another piece
crazy suggests the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A crazy stunt that includes some of life's essentials, but none of the French ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrients are the substances life needs, so they are among its essentials.

clue.text: It can be scorching in Estonia, from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means every other letter is taken from Estonia

explanation.surface: Estonia gets a hot day now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano erupts with scorching lava.

clue.text: Pepper plants 'Desire', putting sticks around

indicators.note: around says the word for sticks goes round the word for desire

parts.note: canes are sticks
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Gardening: support the pepper variety called Desire with canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne pepper plants are a hot chilli species, so these are pepper plants in the plural.

clue.text: Ruminant featured in many a landscape

indicators.note: featured in means the answer appears within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grazing animal shows up in plenty of landscape paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope, which chews the cud like any ruminant.

clue.text: Mysterious store detective thrown out — not vetted unfortunately

indicators.note: thrown out suggests jumbling the letters of the store detective
not says the letters of vetted are left out of that pool
unfortunately reinforces that what remains is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A store detective has been sacked because, unfortunately, he was never vetted.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of VETTED from STORE DETECTIVE, leaving STOREECI, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a select few, so obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Tom's call is about a day somewhere grassy

indicators.note: is about means goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, whose call is a meow

explanation.surface: A tomcat's yowling goes on about a day somewhere grassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is not a man's name but a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of grass is the classic grassy place.

clue.text: … violence and dreadful criminality — resistance is initially futile

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something mangled and in a terrible state, so the letters are rearranged
futile means to no avail, wasted, so these letters are thrown away from the fodder

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word is

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a resistance fighter's slogan that opposing violent criminals is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'futile' removes R (resistance) and I (from 'is initially') from CRIMINALITY, leaving CMINALITY, which 'dreadful' rearranges. 'Resistance is futile' is the borrowed catchphrase hiding the mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Militancy is a readiness to fight or use force for a cause, so aggressive violent action.

clue.text: Passage where 'I will' may be heard?

indicators.note: may be heard says we want a word that sounds like the spoken phrase before it

parts.note: contracted, I will becomes I'll

explanation.surface: A wedding hint: the walk up to the altar is where a bride or groom says 'I will'.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the church walkway where vows are exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway between rows of pews or seats is a passage for walking along.

clue.text: Sister vicious at heart going to ambassador

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: at heart asks for the central letters of the word vicious

explanation.surface: A nun with a cruel streak is sent off to an embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal nuncio is the Pope's diplomatic envoy, the Vatican's ambassador to a country.

clue.text: Single housing worker becomes redundant

indicators.note: housing means containing, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: unwed means not married, single
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A bachelor who puts up a worker finds himself laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redundant is surplus to need, not wanted any longer.

clue.text: They leave EU next, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Speculation about which country will quit the European Union next.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Latin stage direction meaning 'they go out', so 'They leave' is a fair plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction tells several actors to go off stage, literally 'they go out'.

clue.text: Most powerful, content only for some years

indicators.note: content only means keep the inside of the word and drop its first and last letters

parts.note: weightiest means most important or influential, most powerful

explanation.surface: The most powerful are content only for some years.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade such as 1980 to 1989 is a run of some years.

clue.text: Boundary stall leads to argument

parts.note: to hedge is to stall or avoid committing
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A market stall's position along a border sparks a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stall' reads as a market stand, but it is the verb, to evade.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of bushes along a field edge marks its boundary in the English countryside.

clue.text: Moving north, husband and dad start to breed whopping rhubarb

indicators.note: in a down answer, moving north means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sire is a father

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of breed

parts.note: whopping means very big

explanation.surface: A farming scene: a husband and dad move north to breed giant rhubarb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' is not the plant but slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, as is gibberish.

clue.text: Fillet going off?

definitions.meaning: in architecture a fillet is a narrow flat band, a decorative strip
going off means spoiling, becoming covered in fungus

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillet' suggests fish or meat going off, but here it is the architectural band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental strips on walls are fillets, and food that is rotting is growing fungus.

clue.text: Best bit of acrobat's performance?

parts.note: the best part of anything is its peak moment, and an acrobat literally performs high up on a trapeze or wire

explanation.walkthrough: 'acro-' is Greek for high, and an acrobat works aloft, so the best moment is also a lofty location.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the most enjoyable part of an event, and literally a lofty place.

clue.text: A slice of brioche, eh? Awesome in Bray

indicators.note: A slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone in Bray is impressed by a slice of brioche.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'in Bray' as the definition, but 'in' is a link word: the noise a donkey makes is just 'Bray', and Bray reads as the Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's bray is its characteristic loud call.

clue.text: Counter sailor with a short profanity

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a cuss is a swear word

explanation.surface: A sailor at a shop counter swears briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter or a verb, but means a counting device.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads for doing sums is a counting device, so a counter.

clue.text: Trump in South Carolina, and heading for York, dishevelled

parts.note: to ruff is to trump in card games

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of York

explanation.surface: Donald Trump visits South Carolina and then heads for York looking scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the president, but it is the card-game verb; 'in' and 'and' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy and unkempt in appearance is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Fully back service when recruiting Newton — then see

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
back says the word for service is read in reverse

parts.note: a rite is a religious service
N is the abbreviation for newton, the unit of force
Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Full support for a church service that takes on Newton and then a cathedral visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RITE into ETIR; N goes inside to make ENTIR. A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and wholly are synonyms of fully.

clue.text: Primness when undressing is comparatively unsophisticated

indicators.note: undressing means stripping off the outer letters

parts.note: prudery is excessive primness

explanation.surface: A prim person stripping off looks rather unsophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in an old sense means rough or primitive, and the comparative is more so.

clue.text: Resort theatre with character

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: A seaside resort with a theatre full of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday town, but it is the verb: to go somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To resort to a place is an old sense of going there, as in repairing to the bar.

clue.text: Squandered arrival time thus?

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival, written upwards in a down entry gives the first three letters, and the second word of the answer is that instruction, up

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if the time they arrived was wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: ETA, the arrival time, turned up; 'thus?' says the answer describes how those words get written.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or time that has been used up wastefully is consumed or squandered.

clue.text: One echoing 10, like 'Hoy!'

definitions.note: Hoy is an island in Orkney, so like it means an example of its kind

indicators.note: echoing means repeating the sound of another word

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, a passage

explanation.surface: Someone echoes a cry of 'Hoy!'.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is one of the Orkney Islands, off northern Scotland; 'Hoy!' looks like a shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoy is an island in Orkney, a small one of the kind called by this poetic word.

clue.text: After Christ embraces people, there's change

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, dates years after the birth of Christ
men are people

explanation.surface: A Christian message: once Christ embraces people, things change.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or correct, a synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: Ponies fit to travel, notwithstanding …

indicators.note: travel suggests the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ponies are fit to make a journey despite something, the sentence running into 28 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean despite, regardless of something.

clue.text: … cowboy's mount, Lucky, being inclined to recklessness

parts.note: Trigger was the horse of Roy Rogers, the singing cowboy of American films
happy can mean lucky or fortunate, as in a happy accident

explanation.surface: Continuing 27: a cowboy's horse, Lucky, is reckless despite everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucky' looks like the horse's name, but it is the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone too ready to shoot, hence rash and inclined to act without thought.
